335: ### The applier
336: 
337: `scratch/tools/apply_row.py` is the phase 2 script with one added refusal, written in `tasks.md` T005. It reads a ledger path, a row id and an optional root. It refuses a row whose `expected_text` is `OWNED BY PHASE` or `DELETE FILE`. It refuses when the expected text is already in the file, so an append-style row cannot apply twice. It refuses unless the `locator` occurs exactly once. It replaces that one occurrence and prints `APPLIED <id> <file>`. Every refusal prints `FAIL <id>: <reason>` and exits 1.
338: 
339: `scratch/tools/lib.sh` adds `apply_checked`, which prints the applier result and a `CHECK <id> extra_paths=<n>` line. `extra_paths` counts changed paths the row does not name. It must be 0 for every row.
340: 
341: ### Mirror mechanics
342: 
343: | Tree | Role | How it is produced | How it is checked |
344: |------|------|--------------------|-------------------|
345: | `.skilled/commands` | Canonical command source | Authored here | Not generated |
346: | `.opencode/commands` | OpenCode view | Symlink to `.skilled/commands` | `sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs --check` |
347: | `.claude/commands` | Claude view | Per-file symlinks to `.skilled/commands` | `sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs --check` |
348: | `.skilled/agents` | Canonical OpenCode agent source | Authored here, also reached as `.opencode/agents` | Not generated |
349: | `.claude/agents` | Authored Claude sibling | Edited by the six MIRROR rows, no generator | `check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs --all` |
350: | `.cursor/agents`, `.devin/agents` | Cursor and Devin views | Symlinks to `.claude/agents` | `sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs --check` and the roster check |
351: | `.codex/agents` | Codex TOML | `sync-agents.cjs` from `.skilled/agents` | `sync-agents.cjs --check` |
352: | `.codex/prompts` | Codex command stubs | `sync-prompts.cjs` from `.skilled/commands` | `sync-prompts.cjs --check` |
353: | `.pi/agents` | Pi agent copies | `sync-agents-pi.cjs` from `.skilled/agents` | `sync-agents-pi.cjs --check` |
354: | `.pi/prompts` | Pi command stubs | `sync-prompts-pi.cjs` from `.skilled/commands` | `sync-prompts-pi.cjs --check` |
355: 
356: Never hand-edit `.codex`, `.pi`, `.cursor` or `.devin`. Run the generator named in the table. The `.claude/agents` tree is the one authored sibling, and the six MIRROR rows are its scripted edit.

359: `rows.jsonl` goes through `apply_row.py`, one row at a time. Each apply is followed by a changed-path check. The four searches then prove the stale text is gone. The generators rebuild the generated trees, the eight checks prove they agree, and the diff goes through the scope check, the suite comparison and the frontier review.

557: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
558: 
559: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
560: 
561: ### Roles
562: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It runs every command in `tasks.md` and reads every output. It edits only this phase folder plus the files the rows name. It keeps `goal.md` section 4 current.
563: - **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` with `gpt-6-luna` at phase close. It writes nothing.
564: - **Worker**: none. Every text change is frozen in a row and applied by `apply_row.py`, so no model decides what to write in this phase.

566: ### Pre-Task Checklist
567: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first command

572: ### Execution Rules
573: 
574: | Rule | Requirement |
575: |------|-------------|
576: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. No task in this phase is parallel, and at most one dispatch runs at a time |
577: | TASK-SCOPE | A row changes only the file it names. A generator changes only its own output tree |
578: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
579: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
580: | TASK-NOHAND | Never edit a file that a row names by hand. Only `apply_row.py` changes it. Never hand-edit a generated mirror |
581: | TASK-NOJUDGE | A row whose locator is gone is recorded and skipped. The conductor does not rewrite the row and does not ask a model to |
582: | TASK-BANNED | The conductor and the reviewer never run `git commit` outside T014, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |

625: PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
626: ```
627: 
628: `PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.
629: 
630: ### Status Reporting Format
631: 
632: A status line that starts with the task id, then DONE or BLOCKED, then one line of evidence. Write it as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.
633: 
634: ### Blocked Task Protocol
635: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<phase start commit> -- <file>`.
636: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
637: 3. Rerun a failed generator once. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.
638: 4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4.
639: <!-- /ANCHOR:ai-execution -->
640: 
641: ---
642: 
643: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
644: 
645: ### ADR-001: Freeze the audit as exact rows and apply it by script
646: 
647: **Status**: Accepted
648: 
649: **Context**: The audit found 21 stale statements in 12 files. A weak model asked to fix them from a description may reword the new text, change a neighbouring line or skip one. The same text must land in four Claude agent bodies without a second judgment.
650: 
651: **Decision**: Every change is frozen at authoring time as a row with a locator and an exact replacement. `apply_row.py` makes every change and refuses unless the locator occurs exactly once. No model edits a file in this phase.
652: 
653: **Consequences**:
654: - The 27 rows cost no model call, and each one is checked by its own counts.
655: - A second apply fails, so a retry can never edit twice.
656: - A row whose text drifted is skipped and recorded, not guessed.
657: 
658: **Alternatives Rejected**:
659: - A worker reads each file and edits the prose: it can paraphrase, and the audit would then differ from the text this packet reviewed.
660: - `sed -i` one-liners: the quoting of backticks, pipes and quotes in these lines is the exact place a weak model slips, and `sed` replaces every match without a count check.
661: 
662: ### ADR-002: Edit the authored Claude sibling by row, then regenerate the generated trees
663: 
664: **Status**: Accepted
665: 
666: **Context**: `.claude/agents` is an authored tree in the Claude dialect, not a generated one. `.codex` and `.pi` are generated from `.skilled/agents`. Editing `.skilled/agents` alone leaves the Claude body behind, and `check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs` reports drift.
667: 
668: **Decision**: Six MIRROR rows apply the same body text to `.claude/agents`. The `.codex` and `.pi` trees are rebuilt by their generators. No one hand-edits `.codex`, `.pi`, `.cursor` or `.devin`.
669: 
670: **Consequences**:
671: - The agent mirror check passes on the corrected tree.
672: - The Claude sibling stays an authored file, so a future agent change must repeat this two-step shape.
673: 
674: **Alternatives Rejected**:
675: - Hand-edit `.codex/agents/*.toml` and `.pi/agents/*.md`: the next generator run reverts them, and the hand edit hides the drift until then.
676: - Skip the Claude sibling: `check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs --all` fails and the phase cannot close.
677: 
678: ### ADR-003: Compare the suite and the trigger index with the phase start, not with phase 1
679: 
680: **Status**: Accepted
681: 
682: **Context**: Phase 1 recorded `suite-start.txt` before any template changed. Phases 2 to 5 add tests, so a literal match with phase 1 would block on tests this phase did not write. The trigger index is already stale at the phase start for reasons outside this phase, so a freshness gate would block on a pre-existing condition.
683: 
684: **Decision**: The suite gate compares the `Test Files`, `Tests` and `exit=` lines at the phase start with the same lines at close. The trigger-index gate compares the staleness set before and after. Both record the cumulative difference against phase 1 as information, not as a pass condition.
685: 
686: **Consequences**:
687: - A regression this phase introduces is caught.
688: - A known difference from an earlier phase is reported, not mistaken for a defect.
689: - The conductor cannot claim a clean phase-1 match, and the plan says so.
690: 
691: **Alternatives Rejected**:
692: - Require an exact phase-1 match: it fails on the tests phases 2 to 5 added, and a weak executor would then try to delete them.
693: - Require `fresh: true` from the trigger index: the index is stale before the phase starts, so the gate would be red on arrival.

335: ### The applier
336: 
337: `scratch/tools/apply_row.py` is the phase 2 script with one added refusal, written in `tasks.md` T005. It reads a ledger path, a row id and an optional root. It refuses a row whose `expected_text` is `OWNED BY PHASE` or `DELETE FILE`. It refuses when the expected text is already in the file, so an append-style row cannot apply twice. It refuses unless the `locator` occurs exactly once. It replaces that one occurrence and prints `APPLIED <id> <file>`. Every refusal prints `FAIL <id>: <reason>` and exits 1.
338: 
339: `scratch/tools/lib.sh` adds `apply_checked`, which prints the applier result and a `CHECK <id> extra_paths=<n>` line. `extra_paths` counts changed paths the row does not name. It must be 0 for every row.
340: 
341: ### Mirror mechanics
342: 
343: | Tree | Role | How it is produced | How it is checked |
344: |------|------|--------------------|-------------------|
345: | `.skilled/commands` | Canonical command source | Authored here | Not generated |
346: | `.opencode/commands` | OpenCode view | Symlink to `.skilled/commands` | `sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs --check` |
347: | `.claude/commands` | Claude view | Per-file symlinks to `.skilled/commands` | `sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs --check` |
348: | `.skilled/agents` | Canonical OpenCode agent source | Authored here, also reached as `.opencode/agents` | Not generated |
349: | `.claude/agents` | Authored Claude sibling | Edited by the six MIRROR rows, no generator | `check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs --all` |
350: | `.cursor/agents`, `.devin/agents` | Cursor and Devin views | Symlinks to `.claude/agents` | `sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs --check` and the roster check |
351: | `.codex/agents` | Codex TOML | `sync-agents.cjs` from `.skilled/agents` | `sync-agents.cjs --check` |
352: | `.codex/prompts` | Codex command stubs | `sync-prompts.cjs` from `.skilled/commands` | `sync-prompts.cjs --check` |
353: | `.pi/agents` | Pi agent copies | `sync-agents-pi.cjs` from `.skilled/agents` | `sync-agents-pi.cjs --check` |
354: | `.pi/prompts` | Pi command stubs | `sync-prompts-pi.cjs` from `.skilled/commands` | `sync-prompts-pi.cjs --check` |
355: 
356: Never hand-edit `.codex`, `.pi`, `.cursor` or `.devin`. Run the generator named in the table. The `.claude/agents` tree is the one authored sibling, and the six MIRROR rows are its scripted edit.

358: ### Data Flow
359: `rows.jsonl` goes through `apply_row.py`, one row at a time. Each apply is followed by a changed-path check. The four searches then prove the stale text is gone. The generators rebuild the generated trees, the eight checks prove they agree, and the diff goes through the scope check, the suite comparison and the frontier review.

557: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
558: 
559: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
560: 
561: ### Roles
562: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It runs every command in `tasks.md` and reads every output. It edits only this phase folder plus the files the rows name. It keeps `goal.md` section 4 current.
563: - **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` with `gpt-6-luna` at phase close. It writes nothing.
564: - **Worker**: none. Every text change is frozen in a row and applied by `apply_row.py`, so no model decides what to write in this phase.

566: ### Pre-Task Checklist
567: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first command
568: - [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4, never the main checkout

572: ### Execution Rules
573: 
574: | Rule | Requirement |
575: |------|-------------|
576: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. No task in this phase is parallel, and at most one dispatch runs at a time |
577: | TASK-SCOPE | A row changes only the file it names. A generator changes only its own output tree |
578: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
579: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
580: | TASK-NOHAND | Never edit a file that a row names by hand. Only `apply_row.py` changes it. Never hand-edit a generated mirror |
581: | TASK-NOJUDGE | A row whose locator is gone is recorded and skipped. The conductor does not rewrite the row and does not ask a model to |
582: | TASK-BANNED | The conductor and the reviewer never run `git commit` outside T014, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |

The last number is the count of changed lines in the copy, so it proves the applier changed one line and ran only once. Then `bash -n "$PHASE/scratch/tools/lib.sh" && echo SYNTAX_OK` prints `SYNTAX_OK`.
112: 
113:   `apply_row.py` reads a ledger path, a row id and an optional root directory. It refuses a row whose `expected_text` is `OWNED BY PHASE` or `DELETE FILE`. It refuses when the expected text is already in the file, so a second apply cannot append or replace twice. It refuses unless the `locator` occurs exactly once in the row's file. It replaces that one occurrence, prints `APPLIED <id> <file>` and exits 0. Every refusal prints `FAIL <id>: <reason>` and exits 1. The expected-text guard is the reason a second apply fails, because an append-style row keeps its old text as a prefix and the locator alone would still occur once.

117: cat > "$PHASE/scratch/tools/apply_row.py" <<'PY'
118: import json, sys
119: ledger, row_id = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
120: root = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "."
121: rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ledger, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]
122: match = [r for r in rows if r["id"] == row_id]
123: if len(match) != 1:

125: r = match[0]

132: count = text.count(r["locator"])

134:     sys.exit(f"FAIL {row_id}: locator found {count} times in {r['file']}")
135: open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text.replace(r["locator"], r["expected_text"], 1))

111: - [ ] T005 Save the tools, then test the applier on a copy (`scratch/tools/apply_row.py`, `scratch/tools/check_rows.py`, `scratch/tools/lib.sh`). Run the four heredocs below, then the self-test. Verify: the self-test prints, in order, a line that starts with `APPLIED R-001`, a line that starts with `FAIL R-001: expected text already present`, `exit=1`, and `1`. The last number is the count of changed lines in the copy, so it proves the applier changed one line and ran only once. Then `bash -n "$PHASE/scratch/tools/lib.sh" && echo SYNTAX_OK` prints `SYNTAX_OK`.
112: 
113:   `apply_row.py` reads a ledger path, a row id and an optional root directory. It refuses a row whose `expected_text` is `OWNED BY PHASE` or `DELETE FILE`. It refuses when the expected text is already in the file, so a second apply cannot append or replace twice. It refuses unless the `locator` occurs exactly once in the row's file. It replaces that one occurrence, prints `APPLIED <id> <file>` and exits 0. Every refusal prints `FAIL <id>: <reason>` and exits 1. The expected-text guard is the reason a second apply fails, because an append-style row keeps its old text as a prefix and the locator alone would still occur once.
114: 
115: ```bash
116: cd "$WORKTREE"
117: cat > "$PHASE/scratch/tools/apply_row.py" <<'PY'
118: import json, sys
119: ledger, row_id = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
120: root = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "."
121: rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ledger, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]
122: match = [r for r in rows if r["id"] == row_id]
123: if len(match) != 1:
124:     sys.exit(f"FAIL {row_id}: expected 1 ledger row, found {len(match)}")
125: r = match[0]
126: if r["expected_text"] in ("OWNED BY PHASE", "DELETE FILE"):
127:     sys.exit(f"FAIL {row_id}: not a text replacement ({r['expected_text']})")
128: path = f"{root}/{r['file']}"
129: text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
130: if r["expected_text"] in text:
131:     sys.exit(f"FAIL {row_id}: expected text already present in {r['file']}")
132: count = text.count(r["locator"])
133: if count != 1:
134:     sys.exit(f"FAIL {row_id}: locator found {count} times in {r['file']}")
135: open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text.replace(r["locator"], r["expected_text"], 1))
136: print(f"APPLIED {row_id} {r['file']}")
137: PY
138: ```

## 3. SCOPE

### In Scope
- Repair the known template, example and reference defects, found by a census and fixed by exact text swap.
- Gate unfilled placeholders on new docs only, through a template version marker.
- Add a one-line fill instruction with a good and a weak example to each core template section.
- Add a short authoring card and route the skill router to it.
- Check and update the speckit and doctor commands and the doc-authoring agents such as markdown.
- Align the playbook, catalog and READMEs of system-spec-kit, then run the playbooks in a disposable worktree.
- Measure the authoring baseline before any change and again at the end.
- One write-recipe fix, tracked as a child of the earlier write-recipe series.

### Out of Scope
- Any change to `sk-prompt`. All logic lives in system-spec-kit.
- Any change that alters the verdict for an existing packet, because external-repo users would break on `/doctor:update`.
- Measuring models other than DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max for the benchmark.
- Committing or pushing. Both stay with the operator.

### Files to Change

| File Path | Change Type | Phase | Description |
|-----------|-------------|-------|-------------|
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/examples/**` | Modify | 002, 004 | Example descriptions, stale lines, skeleton alignment |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/**` | Modify | 002, 005, 006 | Style guide, checklist, template guide, new card |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/core/*.tmpl` | Modify | 003, 004, 005 | Token form, v2.3 marker, fill guidance, task `Verify:` slot |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-placeholders.sh` and its TypeScript mirror | Modify | 003 | Versioned placeholder gate |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/SKILL.md`, `leaf-manifest.json`, `leaf-aliases.json` | Modify | 005 | Router loads the card |
| `.skilled/commands/speckit/`, `.skilled/commands/doctor/` speckit entries, `.skilled/agents/markdown.md` and other doc-authoring agents | Modify | 006 | Commands and agents match the new templates, gate and card |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/` guard scripts | Create | 004, 005 | Example drift guard and card sync guard |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/manual-testing-playbook/`, `feature-catalog/`, READMEs | Modify | 007 | Scenarios and docs for the new behavior |
| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/` | Create | 008, 009 | Playbook run report and benchmark report |
| `specs/system-speckit/041-write-recipe-fixes/006-fix-write-recipe-move-destination/` | Create | 041-006 | Write-recipe move destination fix |

### Launch preconditions

The operator meets all four before the first phase runs. The conductor records each as met in `goal.md` section 4 and stops when one is not.

1. **Workspace.** The operator chooses A) a git worktree or B) the current branch, following `sk-git`. The conductor never chooses. The chosen path becomes `WORKTREE` in `goal.md` section 4.
2. **Provider login.** `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`. A billing or region refusal stops the run.
3. **Lane authorization.** At most 3 parallel DeepSeek lanes and never two on one file. The operator has already given this.
4. **Conductor placement.** The conductor is a DeepSeek session that runs outside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses self-dispatch and forbids a nested `opencode run`.
